profile.name: Shirasagi Reiji
profile.home: the Shirasagi residence, east of the home street
profile.nature: Cold, exact, principled. Checks his pocket watch more than people check their phones. Cannot forgive a broken promise, including his own. Raised to keep every feeling folded away like a pressed shirt; underneath he is the gentlest person in the school and hates that anyone might notice. Refuses the family car and walks to school, as his father used to walk him. Wears a scarf even in summer.
profile.rumour: The president? Out of the Shirasagi gate at 7:40 sharp - he'd rather die than be at 7:41 - and at the gate by 8:00 to check ties. The housekeeper answers the bell. Pray his mother doesn't.
profile.mio_says: Shirasagi-kun leaves at seven forty. Exactly. His mother watches him go from the upstairs window. She doesn't wave. Fufu. On the thirteenth she doesn't sleep at all.

wait_outside: Behind the white wall of the Shirasagi residence, a gardener rakes gravel into perfect lines.
A black car idles at the gate with its engine running. Nobody gets in.
Through the gate you glimpse a maneki-neko the size of a child, its paw raised. Its paint is cracked.
Upstairs a curtain moves. A woman in a pale kimono looks down at you, then lets the curtain fall.
A grandfather clock inside strikes a quarter. Exactly on time, a door upstairs opens.
The housekeeper's voice: "Young master, your scarf." Reiji's: "I have it, Sawada-san. I always have it."
You hear a short, sharp conversation in the hall. A woman's voice, perfectly calm. Reiji answers 'Yes, Mother' three times.
Koi in the garden pond gather at the edge, waiting for someone who used to feed them.
A row of brand-new straw brooms leans by the servants' door. Next to them, a box of long iron nails.
Reiji's voice, very quietly, to somebody: "...I'll be careful. I'm always careful."
ring_self_low: Reiji opens the gate himself and looks at you as if you were a spelling mistake. "Asagiri. Why are you at my house."
"You rang. At seven thirty-eight. I leave at seven forty. You have two minutes to explain yourself."
"If this is about the incident at school, make an appointment with the council. If it's not, I'm leaving."
"Asagiri." He checks his pocket watch. "You are not on my schedule."
He looks past you at the road, then back. "...Did someone send you? My mother?"
"The bell is for guests. You're not a guest. You're an irregularity."
"I don't need an escort. I've walked to school by myself for five years." A pause. "Since you ask."
"You are in uniform. Your tie is crooked. Fix it before you stand at my gate."
"Do not ring twice. My mother hears the second ring."
"Ah. The transfer student. Who annoys me for no reason. What do you want."
ring_self_mid: Reiji opens the gate, already in his scarf. "Asagiri. You're early. ...That's acceptable."
"You came again." He says it like a reprimand, but he's already closing the gate behind him. "Walk, then."
"Seven thirty-nine. Good. You've learned the value of a minute."
"I suppose you want to walk together. I suppose I'll allow it. Don't talk too much before eight."
"Asagiri. You have rice on your collar. ...Here." He removes it with two fingers.
"Sawada-san said a friend was at the gate. I corrected her. Then I came out anyway."
"You're here. Good. I need someone to tell me if my mother is watching from the window. Don't look. Tell me."
"I thought you'd forget. You didn't. Hm."
"Asagiri. Walk on the outside. If a car comes, you'll be the one it hits, and I'll file the report."
"Do you always ring like that? Like an apology? Ring like you mean it."
ring_self_high: Reiji is waiting just inside the gate. He pretends he wasn't. "Asagiri. On time. ...I'm glad."
"Good morning." It costs him something to say it. He says it anyway. "Let's go."
"You came. You said you would and you came. Do you know how rare that is in this house?"
"I made tea. It's in a flask. There are two cups. That's a coincidence."
"Asagiri." He looks at you a long moment. "Thank you. Don't make me say it twice."
"I've been standing here since seven thirty-five. Don't tell anyone. Especially not Sawada-san. She'd cry."
"You know my father used to walk me to school. Every day. Until... Let's walk."
"Good. You're here. Now the morning has a shape."
"I brought you a scarf. It's cold by the harbour. I don't care if you're cold. I just had a spare."
"Asagiri. I still find you irritating." He almost smiles. "I've decided I don't mind."
ring_parent: An elderly housekeeper in a grey apron bows. "Good morning. You must be Asagiri-sama. The young master will be down in exactly two minutes."
Sawada-san smiles kindly. "A school friend. How lovely. He doesn't have them over. I'll tell him. Please, wait by the koi."
"Asagiri-sama. Please do not ring a second time. Madam is resting." She glances upstairs.
"Ah, the young man from the sweet shop. The young master mentioned you. Well. He said your name in a sentence. That's a lot, for him."
"He's polishing his shoes. He polishes them every morning, though nobody has stepped on them since yesterday."
"Have some tea while you wait. No? Then at least stand out of the rain. The gate roof is wide enough for two."
"I've served this family thirty years. I raised that boy as much as anyone did. Be kind to him. He won't ask."
"He takes his father's watch every morning. He winds it twelve times. Never eleven, never thirteen."

ring_parent.t: A woman in a pale silk kimono opens the door herself. Her smile is perfect. "Asagiri. Haruka's nephew. How nice. Reiji will be down." Her eyes don't move.
"So you are the boy from the train." Mrs. Shirasagi looks at you like a contract she hasn't signed yet. "Reiji. Your visitor."
"Asagiri-kun. Tell me, does the Nekomori child still follow you everywhere?" She smiles. "Never mind. Reiji is coming."
"My son doesn't need company on the road. But he is polite. He will walk with you." The door closes softly in your face.

ring_parent: "The car is ready, as every morning. He'll refuse it, as every morning. His father walked, you see."
"You're early, Asagiri-sama. The young master likes early people. He won't say so. He'll just be less cold."
Sawada-san lowers her voice. "If he looks tired, it's because madam was up late. On certain nights she goes out. Don't ask him about it."
"Please mind the gravel. The gardener lines it every morning. The young master steps only on the stones."
parent_about_you: "Since his father passed, the young master has not had anyone to walk with. You're the first in five years."
"He keeps a box in his wardrobe of presents he never gave anyone. Last week he added something. I wonder who for."
"He's not cold, Asagiri-sama. He's careful. Someone in this house taught him to be."
"He wears the scarf because he's always cold. He's been cold since he was a baby. Strange child. Dear child."
"Madam doesn't approve of the sweet shop. Or the cat shrine. Or anyone, really. Don't take it personally."
"If he snaps at you, he's frightened. He snaps at everyone he likes."
"The master used to say the sea gives Shirasagi everything and takes it back with interest. Then it took him."
"Thank you. I mean it. Come again tomorrow. I'll make extra tea, and he'll pretend not to drink it."
parent_left: "The young master left at seven forty precisely, Asagiri-sama. As always. He looked at the road for a moment first."
"He's gone. He'll be at the school gate by eight checking everyone's ties. Including, I expect, yours."
"I'm sorry, he has already left. He refused the car again. Madam was displeased."
"Gone, I'm afraid. He said, 'If Asagiri comes, tell him he is late.' And then he smiled. I haven't seen that in years."
"He went early for council business. He said nothing about waiting. He waited three minutes anyway."
"You've missed him by a few minutes. If you run, you might see his scarf at the bridge."
parent_evening: "He's in the study with council papers. He'll be there until eleven. Shall I tell him you called?"
"Good evening, Asagiri-sama. The young master is at the piano. He only plays when madam is out. Please don't mention it."
"He's home, but madam has guests. It would be better if you left quietly. I'm sorry."
"He walked home by the harbour again. He always stands at the place his father was found. Then he comes home and says nothing."
"It's the dusk hour. Go home quickly, young man. This house doesn't like the dusk hour."

parent_evening.t: Mrs. Shirasagi answers in a dark coat, a cloth bundle under her arm. "Reiji is studying. You should be home, Asagiri-kun. It's late for boys like you."

come_out_low: Reiji steps through the gate and starts walking without waiting. "Keep up, if you're coming."
"Very well. You may walk beside me. Not in front. Not behind. Beside."
"I'll tell you now: I don't chat before eight. I review the day."
He checks his watch, then the road. "We'll be on time if you don't dawdle. Don't dawdle."
"Why do you keep looking at me? I find you irritating. I have no reason. It's very irritating."
"You walk like someone who's lost something. Stand up straight."
"If anyone asks, we met by chance."
"I'm Shirasagi. Student council president. You know that. I'm saying it so you remember who you're walking with."
come_out_mid: Reiji comes out, adjusting his scarf. "Asagiri. Shall we?"
"Good. You're here. I have three council problems and you will listen to all of them."
"Seven forty. We'll take the harbour road. It's longer. I need the time."
He hands you a small paper cup of tea from his flask without comment.
"I suppose this is a habit now. I don't like habits I didn't choose. I chose this one."
"Walk on the outside. You know the rules."
"You're less irritating in the mornings. Marginally."
come_out_high: Reiji comes out and, without looking at you, falls into step at your exact pace. "Good morning, Asagiri."
"You came. I knew you would. I still checked my watch fourteen times."
"Let's go. Slowly today. I want to see the harbour."
He offers you the second scarf again. When you take it, his ears go faintly red. "It's practical."
"I don't have to explain myself to you. That's what I like about it."
"Asagiri. Do you know you're the only person I don't correct? ...That was a compliment. Don't respond."
"Father used to say 'the road is shorter with company'. I thought it was a figure of speech."
"Good morning." A small, tired smile. "I slept badly. Walk with me and don't ask why."
come_out_rushed: Reiji strides out with his scarf only half tied. "You rang. Before seven forty. Sawada-san made me come down. I hadn't finished my tea."
"Do you know what it means to come early in this house? It means my mother hears." He shuts the gate harder than needed.
"Rushing is a sign of poor planning. Yours, not mine."
"I will be at school at seven fifty-six instead of eight. Four minutes of my life are now yours. Use them well."
He's buttoning his cuff. "Next time, wait. I'm not an alarm clock."
"You rang twice. I told you not to ring twice." He looks up at the window. "...Walk. Now."
"Early is acceptable. Disrupting the house is not. Let's go."
"I'm leaving my father's watch on the desk because of you. I've never done that. Don't make me regret it."
come_out_rain: Reiji opens a large black umbrella. "Rain. Again. The harbour master says the sea's never been this restless in spring."
"Stand under the umbrella. I'm not offering. I'm preventing you from catching a cold and missing council duty."
"You smell of rain all the time, Asagiri. Has anyone told you?"
"The Nekomori boy cried again, didn't he. The whole town gets wet when he does. It's absurd. It's also true."
"My father hated rain. He went out in it anyway. Let's go."
pickup_accept: "Yes. Let's not be late. It would be unbearable to be late with you."
"Walk with me, then. Quietly, if you can manage it."
"Together. Don't make it a big thing."
pickup_decline: "You came all this way to stand at my gate? Bizarre. Good morning, then." He walks off, slightly faster than usual.
"I see. Then I'll go. Don't be late, Asagiri. I'll be at the gate."
"Then why did you ring? ...Never mind. It doesn't matter." It obviously does.
"Fine. I walk alone. I'm used to it."
He looks at his watch for a long time. "Go to school, Asagiri."
walk: "Three students tripped on the east stairs this week. Same step. I measured it. It isn't loose. It isn't anything."
"The student council budget is eleven thousand yen short. Someone is buying a great deal of salt."
"This is the road my father walked me on. He used to name every boat in the harbour. I remember four."
"Don't step on the cracks. Not superstition. Your shoes will scuff."
"You have a strange effect on the Nekomori boy. I want a report on it. Verbally will do."
"The maneki-neko factory is losing money. Since 2010. Exactly since 2010. Nobody wants to say why."
"Inukai runs in the corridors. Every day. He limps afterwards. I've stopped writing him up. Don't tell him."
"Hayase thinks the student council covers things up. The student council is me. I don't cover things up. I file them."
"Kuroe-senpai said my scarf has a face in it. It doesn't. ...Does it?"
"Black tea, no sugar. Sugar is a lie you tell your tongue."
"Why do you keep walking on the road side? I'm not fragile. I'm also not going to swap."
"Makabe-sensei once returned my essay with a single note: 'Feel something.' I filed a complaint."
"The harbour looks peaceful from here. It isn't. Nothing in this town is what it looks like from a distance."
"I've read every school record since 1890. There's a gap in 2010. Two months. Nobody signed anything."
"My mother says the sweet shop is beneath us. Your aunt's mochi is the best thing I've eaten in a year. Both are true."
"Late people tell themselves a minute doesn't matter. Then a minute becomes a life."
"You smell of rain and old paper. My grandmother smelled like that. Before she stopped talking."
"I'm told I have no sense of humour. That's untrue. I simply don't share it with people who aren't funny."
"The vending machine by the bridge overcharges. I've reported it. Twice. It's still overcharging. It's personal now."
"If you ever lie to me, Asagiri, I won't shout. I'll just stop talking to you. Forever. It's very efficient."
"Look. A heron. Shirasagi means white heron. My family put it on everything. Even the bento boxes."
"I counted the six Jizo at the crossroads once. I got seven. I counted again and got six. I haven't counted since."
"Do you play shogi? You look like you'd lose gracefully. That's a rare quality."
"The school roof is closed after six. If I find you there after six, I'll lock you on it."
"My mother wants me to run the company. My father wanted me to be a teacher. I want to sleep for a week."
"I was given a car for my sixteenth birthday. I've never sat in it. It's very clean."
"Your tie's crooked again. ...No, leave it. It suits your general disorder."
"The fishermen say there are lights out at sea. My mother had the harbour fenced off. She doesn't explain."
"I keep my father's watch five minutes fast. He did. I've never set it right. I never will."
"Why does Inukai growl at you? He doesn't. He growls at everyone else near you. Interesting."
"I've been told I walk like a funeral. I prefer 'like a procession'."
"Have you noticed the town's cats all look at us when we pass? Like inspectors."
"I don't dislike you. I dislike that I can't explain why I dislike you. That's different."
"If you ever need something from the council, ask me. Directly. Not through the Ura board. I hate that board."
"There's a box in my room. Gifts I never gave. Don't ask what's in it. ...Ask me in a year."
"The harbour bell rang by itself last week. At four in the morning. My mother was out. She came back soaked."
"Promise me you'll never make a promise you can't keep. That includes this one."
"I know the names of everyone in this school. I don't use them. Names are a responsibility."
"The morning sea is the only thing in Suzunari that's honest. It's grey and it says so."
"We're at the bridge at seven fifty-two. Two minutes ahead. You're improving."
walk_close: "My father drowned at the harbour five years ago. On a calm night. He was a strong swimmer. I've never said that to anyone but the police."
"On the thirteenth of every month my mother goes out at two in the morning. She takes a hammer. I lie awake and count until she's back."
"I wear the scarf because I'm always cold. I dream of snow. Somebody leaving me in snow and not coming back."
"You irritate me because I feel I've waited for you before. A long time. And you didn't come. That's insane. I know."
"I've never been thanked by my mother. Not once. I don't want to be. I just want to know what it would sound like."
"If I have to choose between my family and what's right, I don't know what I'll do. I need you to know I don't know."
"I'm not cold. I'm folded. Someone folded me very small a long time ago and I've never found the edges."
"The box of gifts. There's one for you now. Don't ask. I'll give it when I'm brave."
"You're the first person since my father who walks at my pace without being told."
"The Nekomori boy. Whatever happens with him, be honest with him. Honesty is the only kindness I trust."
"I like this. The walking. Don't say anything. If you say something it becomes a conversation, and conversations end."
"If one day I'm not at the gate at eight, come and find me. I mean it. I don't say things I don't mean."
"My mother thinks the Nekomori boy is the reason we're losing everything. I think we lost it a long time before him."
"I've decided I trust you. It's a decision, not a feeling. Decisions last longer."
"Asagiri. Thank you. There. Now don't ever mention it."
walk_rain: "The gutters are overflowing. I'll write to the council. I am the council. I'll write to myself."
"Stay under the umbrella. Your shoulder's wet. ...Closer, then. Practically."
"The harbour will be closed. The boats are tied twice. My father always said tie twice, then a third time for luck."
"Rain like this, you can't hear footsteps. I don't like that. Walk where I can see you."
"Don't step in that. Too late. Your sock is now a disciplinary matter."
"Somebody in this town is very sad. I'd like to fine them for it. I'd also like to help. Both."
arrive: "Eight o'clock. Exactly. Good." He turns to the gate and becomes the president again.
"Go in. I have ties to check. Yours included. ...Yours is fine. Go."
"Thank you for the company. I'm saying it once. Don't expect it daily."
"We're on time. Remember this feeling. It's the only reliable one."
He stops at the gate and adjusts your collar without asking. "Presentable. Go."
"Asagiri. Don't trip on the east stairs. I mean that literally."
"Same time tomorrow?" He hears himself. "...If it's convenient. For the record."
"That was acceptable. Better than acceptable. Go away now."
ask_tell: "Seven forty. Out the gate. Never seven forty-one. Ring once. Sawada-san will answer. If my mother answers, be polite and leave quickly."
"I leave at seven forty and arrive at eight. It's not a secret. It's a schedule. ...You'll come? Then come on time."
"Seven forty. If you're coming, don't be late. I don't wait for late people. I'll wait three minutes for you. That's my limit."
"Why do you - fine. Seven forty. The gate with the white heron crest. Don't ring twice."
"Seven forty precisely. My father left the house at that time for twenty years. I keep it."
ask_refuse: "My movements are not public information, Asagiri."
"Why would you need to know that? If it's council business, submit it in writing."
"No. People who know my schedule report it to my mother."
"Earn it. Keep three promises in a row and ask me again."
"I don't give my schedule to people I'm not sure about. I'm not sure about you. Irritatingly."
"Ask the Ura board. They seem to know everything else. ...Don't ask the Ura board."
home_offer: "Asagiri. You're walking home alone at Omagatoki? Unacceptable. I'll walk you. It's on the way. It isn't."
"The council finished early. I have twenty minutes. I'll walk you home. Efficiently."
"It's getting dark. Your aunt would be worried. I'm not worried. Your aunt would be. Come."
"I'll see you to the sweet shop. I want to buy mochi for Sawada-san. That's the only reason."
"Walk with me as far as your house. I don't want to go home yet. Don't ask why."
"You look like someone who'd answer if his name was called at dusk. I'll walk you."
home_accept: "You'll walk me home? ...I don't need it. But fine. By the harbour road."
"Very well. You can carry the council minutes. They're heavy. That's the honest reason."
"Yes. Please." He looks surprised at himself. "I mean - acceptable."
"Walk me home, then. Stop at the gate. Don't come in. My mother is home."
"Fine. But we walk at my pace." His pace turns out to be yours.
"Nobody's walked me home since my father. ...Let's go before I change my mind."
home_refuse: "No. I have council business until six. And I don't need an escort."
"Not today. My mother sends the car on Thursdays and I can't refuse it twice a week."
"Absolutely not. People would talk. I'd have to discipline them."
"I walk alone. I prefer it. I'm almost sure I prefer it."
"Ask me again when you've stopped being irritating. That might be never."
"No, Asagiri. Not because of you. Because of my house."
home_walk: "The harbour at dusk. My father used to say the boats come home on the last of the light, like children."
"Yuyake Koyake at five. I used to hate that song. It meant going home."
"The sea's red. Don't say it's beautiful. Everyone says it's beautiful. It's just red." A pause. "It's beautiful."
"I counted the steps from the school to my gate once. Two thousand and twelve. With you it feels like less."
"I'm going to the harbour first. Just for a minute. You don't have to stand with me. ...Thank you for standing with me."
"The streetlights on the harbour road were installed by my grandfather. Half of them are broken. My mother won't fix them."
"Omagatoki. When you can't tell people from things. I've always been able to tell. That's my curse."
"I didn't hate today. Write that down. It may not happen again."
"Sawada-san will have tea waiting. She'll ask about you. I'll tell her you're adequate."
"You walk slower in the evening. So do I. It's the light."
"The crows are going to the cat shrine. My mother hates crows. She hates the shrine more."
"Have you noticed the Nekomori boy waits at the shrine steps at dusk? He's waiting for someone to come home. I know the look."
"If you ever see my mother out at night, don't speak to her. Walk away. Please."
"My father whistled on this road. Mio says don't whistle at dusk. I never whistle. I miss it."
"Look at the herons on the breakwater. White heron. Shirasagi. They stand very still and wait. Family trait."
"You're quiet. That's acceptable. I've had enough words today."
"The box of gifts. I'm adding something tonight. Don't ask."
"If I don't say goodbye at the gate, it's because I don't like the word. Not because I don't like you."
"The sweet potato truck plays its song on Fridays. My father bought me one every Friday. I still listen for it."
"I've decided this walk is part of my schedule now. You've been entered."
goodbye: "Here. Thank you, Asagiri. Go home before it gets dark. Don't take the harbour road."
He stops at the gate and does not look back. "Tomorrow. Seven forty. ...Goodnight."
"Sawada-san is waving at you. Ignore her. Wave back. Fine."
"That was... I don't have a word for it. Pleasant. Don't repeat that."
"Go. My mother is at the window. Don't look up."
"Goodnight, Asagiri. You were on time all day. I noticed."
"Thank you for walking at my pace." He goes in before you can answer.
"Don't stand there. Go home. Text me when you arrive. Not a sticker. Words."
"I'll see you at the gate tomorrow. Check your tie."
amane_cut_in: Reiji stops. "Nekomori. You're following us. That's a council matter." Amane flinches. Reiji's voice softens by one degree. "...Walk with us, then. Properly."
"First-year. You're crying in uniform on a public road. ...Here." He hands Amane a folded handkerchief without looking at him.
"Nekomori. I'm not taking anything of yours. I don't take things. My mother does."
He narrows his eyes at the rain. "This is you, isn't it. All of it. Stop it. ...Please."
"You can walk on Asagiri's other side. I have no objection. I object to a lot of things. Not this."
"Nekomori-kun. Your bell is ringing. It's very loud. Do you know my mother can hear it from our house?"
Reiji steps back half a pace, as if giving up a seat. "Go on. He came for you anyway. Everyone can see it."
"Don't glare at me, first-year. I'm the president. I get glared at professionally."
"I'll walk ahead. You two... sort yourselves out. Quickly. We'll be late."
"Nekomori. If something happens to anyone on the east stairs this week, I'll know where to look. I hope I'm wrong."
offer_pickup: "Asagiri. Tomorrow I'll call at your house. Seven thirty-five. Be ready. I don't wait."
"Let me pick you up tomorrow. You're always two minutes late and it's affecting my mornings."
"I'll come by Asagiri-do tomorrow. The sweet shop is on the harbour road if you walk the long way. I'll walk the long way."
"Tomorrow, wait at your door. I'll ring once. Only once."
"My father used to collect me for school. Tomorrow I'll collect you. Don't make a thing of it."
"I'm proposing a schedule change. I pick you up. You don't argue. Agreed?"
at_your_door: Reiji is standing outside Asagiri-do with his watch open. "Seven thirty-five. You're awake. Good. Let's go."
"Your aunt offered me mochi. I accepted two. Don't tell my mother. Come."
He's re-straightening the shop's noren. "It was crooked. Like your tie. Good morning."
"I said I'd come, and I came. That's how promises work. Shall we?"
"Good morning, Asagiri. You have toothpaste on your chin. ...There. Let's go."
"Seven thirty-five. I've been here since seven thirty. That's irrelevant. Walk."
promise_yes: "Tomorrow. Seven forty. A promise." He writes it in his diary in ink. "Now it's binding."
"You promise? Then I'll wait three minutes. Not four. Three."
"I don't make promises lightly. Neither should you. ...Agreed."
"Fine. Tomorrow. If you break it, I'll never ask again. Just so you know the stakes."
promise_broken: "You said seven forty. I waited until seven forty-three. Then I left. I don't wait for broken promises. I waited three minutes for yours."
"Don't explain. Explanations are how people make broken promises feel smaller. It isn't small."
"I wrote it in ink, Asagiri. In ink."
He doesn't look at you. "My father never once broke a promise to me. Not one. Except the last."

Mon: "Monday. Council meeting at lunch. I'll be unbearable. More than usual."
Tue: "Tuesday. The harbour market. My father bought tangerines there. Every Tuesday."
Wed: "Wednesday. Inspection day. Your tie will be judged. I am the judge."
Thu: "Thursday. The car day. My mother insists. I'm walking anyway."
Fri: "Friday. The sweet potato truck tonight. Don't mention it. I'm not interested." He is.
